02 · Quantification

Load packages

pacman::p_load(here, limpa, limma, tibble, writexl)
here::i_am("01_Preprocess/02_Quantification/a_script/02_quantify.qmd")

Read measurements and protein estimates

y holds the filtered precursors from 01_Filtering. proteins holds the protein estimates and their standard errors that 02_quantify_run.R saved, because dpcQuant() takes about 100 minutes and this notebook should render in minutes. The checkpoint must have used every filtered precursor; if filtering changes, rerun the script.

y <- readRDS(here("01_Preprocess", "01_Filtering", "c_data", "precursors_filtered.rds"))

checkpoints <- here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "quant_runs")
sensitivity_file <- file.path(checkpoints, "proteins_slope_fitted.rds")
proteins <- readRDS(file.path(checkpoints, "proteins_slope_0.7.rds"))
stopifnot(sum(proteins$genes$NPrec) == nrow(y))

Missingness

In DIA data, low-intensity precursors go missing more often. The plot shows each precursor’s proportion of missing values against its mean observed intensity; a downward trend is that association.

plotAveVsMis(y)

Fit the detection curve

The detection probability curve (DPC) gives the probability that a precursor is observed as a function of its true intensity, through an intercept and a slope. The dpc() default, model = "cn", is dpcCN(), the complete-normal estimator the limpa FAQ recommends for noisy data, fitted on a stratified subset of 2,000 precursors.

dpcest <- dpc(y$E)
plotDPC(dpcest)
dpc_parameters <- tibble(intercept = dpcest$dpc[1], slope = dpcest$dpc[2])
round(dpc_parameters, 3)
# A tibble: 1 × 2
  intercept slope
      <dbl> <dbl>
1     -8.76 0.478

The fitted slope, 0.478, sits below the 0.7 to 0.9 band the limpa FAQ calls typical for DIA-NN with match-between-runs. The FAQ’s advice for that case is the project’s choice for the primary run: “If dpcCN() doesn’t give a value in that range, it would be reasonable to run dpcQuant() with a preset value dpc.slope=0.7.” Standard errors or hit counts alone do not show which slope is right, so the fitted slope is kept as a sensitivity run (below and in 02_Differential).

Roll-up

02_quantify_run.R combines precursors into proteins with dpcQuant(), grouping by Protein.Group. It returns a complete matrix, an abundance for every protein in every sample, plus a standard error per value; dpcDE() later uses those to predict each protein’s variance. The loaded checkpoint holds 3,451 protein groups from 47,201 precursors. The curve it used, slope preset and intercept estimated by limpa:

round(proteins$dpc, 3)
  beta0   beta1 
-12.915   0.700

Detection filter

filterByDetection() keeps a protein detected in at least n.samples samples. Its help page leaves the threshold to the analyst for a large dataset; here it is the smallest group size. The count runs across all samples, so it does not guarantee detection within any one group.

group_sizes <- table(proteins$targets$group)
detected <- filterByDetection(proteins, n.samples = min(group_sizes))
proteins <- proteins[detected, ]

detection_summary <- data.frame(
  before = length(detected), kept = sum(detected), dropped = sum(!detected),
  minimum_samples = min(group_sizes)
)

group_sizes

 BFR_T1  BFR_T2 HLRT_T1 HLRT_T2 
     33      32      33      33 
detection_summary
  before kept dropped minimum_samples
1   3451 3042     409              32

Normalisation

Cyclic loess (normalizeBetweenArrays(method = "cyclicloess")) removes abundance-dependent differences between samples. DIA-NN normalised the precursors already; this second pass works on the protein estimates. Smyth recommends quantile or cyclic loess normalisation of limpa protein quantifications when sample differences are technical (Bioconductor support).

unnormalised <- proteins$E
proteins$E <- normalizeBetweenArrays(proteins$E, method = "cyclicloess")

Intensity distributions before and after. Then mean-difference (MD) plots for the sample whose median sat furthest from the others before normalisation: each protein’s difference from the mean of the other samples against its average abundance.

sample_medians <- apply(unnormalised, 2, median)
worst <- which.max(abs(sample_medians - median(sample_medians)))
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plotDensities(unnormalised, legend = FALSE, main = "Before cyclic loess")
plotDensities(proteins$E, legend = FALSE, main = "After cyclic loess")
plotMD(unnormalised, column = worst, main = paste(colnames(unnormalised)[worst], "before"))
plotMD(proteins$E, column = worst, main = paste(colnames(proteins$E)[worst], "after"))

Only proteins$E changes. Cyclic loess subtracts an abundance-dependent offset from each value without rescaling it, so the standard errors still apply; the fitted offset is treated as known.

Check protein estimates

Per protein: precursor count (NPrec, which dpcQuant() writes although its help page says NPeptides), proportion observed, mean log2 abundance, mean standard error and mean observed precursors per sample.

protein_quality <- tibble(
  protein = rownames(proteins),
  gene = proteins$genes$Genes,
  n_precursors = proteins$genes$NPrec,
  prop_observed = proteins$genes$PropObs,
  mean_log2 = rowMeans(proteins$E),
  mean_standard_error = rowMeans(proteins$other$standard.error),
  mean_n_observations = rowMeans(proteins$other$n.observations)
)
summary(protein_quality[c("mean_log2", "mean_standard_error", "prop_observed")])
   mean_log2     mean_standard_error prop_observed    
 Min.   :12.98   Min.   :0.03108     Min.   :0.03716  
 1st Qu.:16.07   1st Qu.:0.38547     1st Qu.:0.30245  
 Median :17.10   Median :0.58461     Median :0.42324  
 Mean   :17.52   Mean   :0.65933     Mean   :0.43276  
 3rd Qu.:18.63   3rd Qu.:0.91543     3rd Qu.:0.54962  
 Max.   :26.78   Max.   :1.50295     Max.   :0.97710

plotMDSUsingSEs() places samples by their protein profiles, weighting by the standard errors; each point is labelled with its participant. A sample far from its own participant’s other samples is worth a look. Then the share of the first coordinate that participant and group each explain.

mds <- plotMDSUsingSEs(proteins, labels = proteins$targets$participant, cex = 0.6)
round(sapply(proteins$targets[c("participant", "group")], function(f) {
  summary(lm(mds$x ~ factor(f)))$r.squared
}), 3)
participant       group 
      0.515       0.027

Slope sensitivity

The sensitivity run quantifies against the whole fitted curve, where the primary run passes dpc.slope = 0.7 and lets limpa fit the intercept. Both get the same detection filter, which reads only observation counts and so keeps the same proteins, and the same normalisation. The table gives each run’s curve and mean standard error; the median absolute abundance difference follows. It measures how far values move; 02_Differential compares the contrasts.

sensitivity <- readRDS(sensitivity_file)
sensitivity <- sensitivity[filterByDetection(sensitivity, n.samples = min(group_sizes)), ]
sensitivity$E <- normalizeBetweenArrays(sensitivity$E, method = "cyclicloess")
stopifnot(identical(rownames(sensitivity), rownames(proteins)))

tibble(
  role = c("primary", "sensitivity"),
  intercept = round(c(proteins$dpc[1], sensitivity$dpc[1]), 3),
  slope = round(c(proteins$dpc[2], sensitivity$dpc[2]), 3),
  mean_standard_error = round(c(
    mean(proteins$other$standard.error), mean(sensitivity$other$standard.error)
  ), 3)
)
# A tibble: 2 × 4
  role        intercept slope mean_standard_error
  <chr>           <dbl> <dbl>               <dbl>
1 primary        -12.9  0.7                 0.659
2 sensitivity     -8.76 0.478               0.526
round(median(abs(proteins$E - sensitivity$E)), 4)
[1] 0.2458

The section runs only when c_data/quant_runs/proteins_slope_fitted.rds exists. It takes a separate quantification run:

Rscript 01_Preprocess/02_Quantification/a_script/02_quantify_run.R --sensitivity

Save results

proteins.rds keeps abundance, standard errors, annotations and sample metadata together for every later stage. 02_quantify.xlsx holds the samples, the diagnostic curve fit, detection counts and per-protein quality.

out <- here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data")
saveRDS(proteins, file.path(out, "proteins.rds"))
write_xlsx(
  list(
    samples = as.data.frame(proteins$targets),
    dpc_parameters = dpc_parameters,
    detection_summary = detection_summary,
    protein_quality = protein_quality
  ),
  file.path(out, "02_quantify.xlsx")
)
